In the experiment backed by Robert F. Kennedy Jr., thousands of infants in Guinea-Bissau are to be denied the hepatitis B vaccine for the first six weeks after birth.

A disturbing vaccine experiment backed by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has been facing accusations of eugenics and has garnered comparisons to the racist Tuskegee syphilis experiment — yet it’s moving forward in the African nation of Guinea-Bissau.

So continues the Trump administration’s fundamentally racist strategy when it comes to Africa, a continent the president and his allies have sought to exploit and strip of its resources, from precious minerals to health data.

I wrote about the Kennedy-backed experiment — in which thousands of African infants are to be denied the hepatitis B vaccine for the first six weeks after birth — back in January. Around that time, it was suspended by African officials amid outrage over the project’s ethics and its similarities with eugenics and the deadly Tuskegee experiment, which saw hundreds of Black men denied syphilis treatment for decades in the name of medical experimentation, starting in the 1930s.

To be clear, questions about the safety of the hepatitis B vaccine for newborns have already been asked and answered in the affirmative by reputable scientists.

Regardless, The Guardian reported that the experiment, which is funded partly by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, moved forward last week after gaining approval from the ethics committee overseeing the Danish researchers conducting the study. Several committee members resigned in protest after the vote, including founding member Stig Børsen Hansen, who told the outlet:

“You are now enrolling newborns in a lottery to test a hypothesis,” Hansen said. The children who are randomly selected not to receive the birth dose of the vaccine, those who “lost the lottery,” face in their earliest days the risk of contracting hepatitis B, which can cause irreversible lifelong damage. “They contract hepatitis B in the context of being part of a research project,” Hansen said, which made their infection happen, in effect, “by design.”

The outlet also quotes an infectious disease doctor as saying Kennedy is effectively taking advantage of African children:

Kennedy “wants to make it so we don’t use a birth dose here in this country,” said Paul Offit, an infectious disease physician at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia. “That’s the goal.”

Kennedy would never be able to do the trial in the US because of its significant ethical concerns, Offit added. “He’s taking advantage of a developing country … Is it because children in Africa are more expendable than children here?”

Offit’s skepticism about the bias that appears to be at the heart of this study is well-earned. Kennedy has faced criticism for peddling racist pseudoscience before — including last year, when Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, D-Md., took him to task for claiming that Black people have different immune systems and therefore shouldn’t be on the same vaccine schedule as white people. Dr. Demetre Daskalakis, a top infectious disease expert who resigned from the CDC last year, said in his resignation letter that eugenics “plays prominently in the rhetoric being generated” at Kennedy’s agency.

Spending American tax dollars to run a potentially deadly experiment on African babies obviously isn’t going to dispel those allegations.

Ja'han Jones

Ja’han Jones is an MS NOW opinion blogger. He previously wrote The ReidOut Blog.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Trump says he's considering firing Kimberly Guilfoyle as he brutally admits: 'We're not happy'

President Donald Trump has revealed his feelings about the latest controversies swirling around the US Ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle.

Actual Article Body:
By VICTORIA CHURCHILL, US POLITICAL REPORTER and ELINA SHIRAZI, US SENIOR POLITICAL REPORTER

Published:  08:22 AEDT, 13 October 2026   |  Updated:  09:46 AEDT, 13 October 2026

President Donald Trump said Monday he's weighing ousting his US ambassador to Greece.

Speaking with reporters on the way to his rally in Youngstown, Ohio, Trump shared that he was considering axing Kimberly Guilfoyle, before adding, 'Yeah. We're not happy,' when asked about her conduct.

His remarks came a day after a US official said Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio were 'extremely pissed off' over a string of allegations against Guilfoyle, and would likely decide her fate this week.

Rubio was said to be particularly furious. He visited Athens just last week, where Guilfoyle attended some of his events and greeted him on arrival with a bear hug as the allegations swirled.

A series of reports has alleged that Guilfoyle threatened a host country official, accepted improper gifts and services and offered to use her influence inside the administration in return for payment of a large credit card bill.

On Thursday, the top Democrats on the Senate and House foreign affairs committees urged Rubio to investigate, citing the Journal's reporting.

'If these reports are accurate, Ambassador Guilfoyle is unfit to represent the United States abroad and should be removed from her position,' wrote Representative Gregory Meeks of New York, the top House Foreign Affairs Democrat.

An embassy official said last month that Guilfoyle 'continues to follow all State Department ethical guidelines.'

Kimberly Guilfoyle and President Trump at the Greek Independence Day event in the East Room at the White House in March of 2025

Secretary of State Marco Rubio (R) and US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle (L) unveil a commemorative plaque during a ceremony marking the renovation and opening of a new wing of the US Embassy in Athens, Greece last week

The Daily Mail has also exclusively reported that her party girl lifestyle has landed Guilfoyle in hot water with members of Trump's family.

Trump-world insider Eric Deters, who Guilfoyle reportedly asked for a six-figure payment, told the Daily Mail that she recruited Deters' wife and her friend to secretly sneak alcohol to her during a political festival, acting 'like a high schooler' hiding booze from her parents.

When the event ended, Guilfoyle insisted on packing up all the leftover catered VIP food to take home, Deters said.

He added that she begged him to compliment her in front of Donald Trump Jr, her former fiancé, in the hope of 'winning back his favor.'

The pair ended their engagement in late 2024, and Trump Jr is now with Bettina Anderson.

US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle arrives at the White House on February 26, 2026 in Washington, DC

Guilfoyle's affinity for Champagne and parties have widely been documented, and insiders urged her to be on good behavior after she was tapped to be President Donald Trump's Greek Ambassador, cautioning that an assignment amid Aegean islands and endless summers wasn't a green light for nonstop partying.

Guilfoyle’s lawyers have hit back at the allegations, insisting the dispute with Deters concerns unpaid work rather than an attempt to sell access to the administration.

In a statement reported Monday, they said he owed her approximately $150,000 for speaking engagements and consulting work performed in 2024 and early 2025.

Still, Republicans have begun to sour on Guilfoyle, with Senate Majority Whip John Barasso telling CBS anchor Margaret Brennan on Face The Nation Sunday that the reports about the ambassador were ‘very troubling,’ as well as ‘concerning.’

He added that he expected the State Department to conduct an investigation into the ambassador, before noting that ‘the Senate Foreign Relations Committee will have oversight and look into that as well.’
